question.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: $$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}+t+3 \\ -{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}] $$ The complementary solution to this system is given by $$ {x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R. $$ Then, the general solution of the system is
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+\,\,$ $1$ $\,\,{t}^{2}+\,\,$ $2$ $\,\,t+\,\,$ {{field-1}} .
{{field-2}} {{field-3}} $1$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}+t+3 \\ -{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is polynomial of degree $2.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also polynomial of degree $2,$ i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}{t}^{2}+{b}_{1}t+{c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}{t}^{2}+{b}_{2}t+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]{t}^{2}+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}{t}^{2}+{b}_{1}t+{c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}{t}^{2}+{b}_{2}t+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}+t+3 \\ -{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-({a}_{2}{t}^{2}+{b}_{2}t+{c}_{2}) \\ {a}_{1}{t}^{2}+{b}_{1}t+{c}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}+t+3 \\ -{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0{t}^{2}+2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 0{t}^{2}+2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(-{a}_{2}+2){t}^{2}+(-{b}_{2}+1)t+(-{c}_{2}+3) \\ ({a}_{1}-1){t}^{2}+({b}_{1}+2)t+{c}_{1}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding coefficients of like powers of $t,$ we get the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{a}_{2}+2=0 \\ -\,{b}_{2}+1=2{a}_{1} \\ -\,{c}_{2}+3={b}_{1} \\ {a}_{1}-1=0 \\ {b}_{1}+2=2{a}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}={b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first and fourth equations, we get

$$
{a}_{2}=2,\,{a}_{1}=1.
$$

Substituting these into the second and fifth equations, and solving for ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2},$ we get

$$
{b}_{2}=-1,\,{b}_{1}=2.
$$

Finally, substituting these last values into the third and sixth equations, and solving for ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2},$ we have

$$
{c}_{2}=1,\,{c}_{1}=-1.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+2t-1 \\ 2{t}^{2}-t+1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{t}^{2}+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
